title: KV cache coherence protocol - scratch notes
content:
Purpose / problem statement:
This is a personal scratchpad exploring a light-weight, practical coherence protocol for the KV caches used by Redwood's serving runtime. We need something cheaper than full distributed transactions but stronger than pure eventual consistency for common LLM inference patterns (prefix reuse, KV cache warmups, session handoffs). Target customers: Hosted and Dedicated; private deployments may adopt a stronger variant.

Design goals (prioritized):
- Low p99 latency added to token generation path (<0.5ms target for local checks)
- High hit rate for prefix reuse in typical chat workloads (small edits, long context)
- Predictable behavior during failover / migration (session resume across nodes)
- Graceful degradation: allow stale reads for latency-critical paths, but provide quick invalidation when safety/regeneration is required
- Operational simplicity: debuggable traces and small number of state transitions

Assumptions / constraints:
- Runtime nodes hold per-session KV shards (per-model, per-tenant partitioning).
- There is a control plane (or leader) component that can tag a session node as owner; but we cannot assume a global leader for every request.
- Network partitions happen; need sensible defaults for offline nodes (e.g., local reads allowed, write-backs queued)
- Workloads: many short chat sessions with frequent incremental token additions + occasional rewrites (regeneration)

Core primitives (informal):
- Lease: node acquires short-lived lease for a session's KV shard (lease_id, expires_at). Leases are cheap (non-blocking) and refreshed on active traffic.
- Version vector (vclock-lite): small integer epoch per session plus a per-node last-applied counter. Not full vector clocks, just used to detect obvious divergence.
- Invalidation marker: single key per session that flips to force readers to ignore cached prefixes older than X.
- Write-ahead delta log: ephemeral append-only delta stream for recent KV changes kept for N minutes to allow fast catch-up during handoff.

Fast-path (typical token generation):
1) Ingress node routes request to owning node if known (session-affinity header). If owner unknown, use consistent-hash fallback + probe.
2) Generating node checks local KV cache for required prefix entry. If present and vclock matches, use it.
3) If missing, try read-through to remote owner over short RPC (sync), or if owner unreachable, try replaying local deltas or fall back to recompute from model (expensive).

Handoff / migration (session move):
- When control-plane wants to move session S from node A -> B (scaling, preemption):
  a) Control plane issues a transfer request: B requests a lease transfer; A marks session 'handoff-in-progress' and pauses accepting writes that would break linearization.
  b) A streams the delta log (last M minutes) then final snapshot of compacted KV to B. Both nodes exchange final epochs.
  c) B installs snapshot and accepts new lease; control plane flips owner annotation.
- Avoid blocking live generation: allow A to continue serving reads until lease expiry, but force reconciliation after swap.

Invalidation and regeneration semantics:
- Regeneration request (user hits regenerate): must ensure subsequent tokens do not reuse stale cached KV entries that rely on dropped context. Strategy: generate an incrementing invalidate_token for the session; nodes seeing a regenerate flag will treat cached entries older than invalidate_token as invalid and either re-request or recompute.
- For safety-critical tools (tool-calling or functions) provide a "strong" path that forces owner-roundtrip verification (adds latency but guarantees correctness).

Staleness tradeoffs and config knobs (runtime-config candidates):
- prefer_stale_reads: boolean (default true for latency SLOs)
- max_stale_age_ms: how old a local cache entry may be before rejecting (default 30000)
- delta_log_retention_ms: how long to keep per-session deltas (default 5min)
- lease_ttl_ms and lease_grace_ms: tuning for rapid failover vs noisy renewals

API shapes (sketches) - plain text proto-like shapes: 
- LeaseAcquire(session_id, node_id) -> { success: bool, lease_id: str, expires_at: iso_ts, epoch: int }
- LeaseRefresh(session_id, lease_id, node_id) -> { success: bool, expires_at }
- GetKV(session_id, key, want_epoch) -> { found: bool, value: bytes, epoch: int, invalidated: bool }
- AppendDelta(session_id, delta_blob, from_epoch) -> { ack: bool, new_epoch }
- SnapshotFetch(session_id, from_epoch) -> { snapshot_blob, snapshot_epoch, deltas: [delta_blob] }
- Invalidate(session_id, invalidate_token, reason) -> { ack: bool }

Example call flow for move with minimal disruption (ASCII timeline):

[control] -> request move S from A -> B
B -> A : LeaseAcquire(S,B)  // request handoff
A : mark 'handoff-in-progress', stop non-idempotent writes
A -> B : SnapshotFetch(S, epoch=E0)  // send compacted snapshot + deltas
B : apply snapshot, deltas => epoch E1
control : set owner(S)=B + invalidate_token++ // flip owner in quick metadata store
A : continue serving reads until lease expires; after lease expiry cancels local writes

Questions / open trade-offs (notes to self):
- Should we make lease acquisition optimistic (B assumes role immediately) or conservative (wait til A ack)? Optimistic reduces downtime but risks split-brain. Maybe use short overlap window and rely on invalidate_token to reconcile.
- Delta log sizing: keeping deltas for long helps handoff but costs memory; 5–10 minutes seems reasonable for typical chat but heavy rewrite workloads (notebooks) may need adjustments.
- How to surface debugging info? need per-session timeline visible in Console: last-owner, last-leased-at, invalidate-token, delta-count, last-snapshot-ts.
- Could we piggyback deltas on existing tracing/telemetry pipeline to avoid extra RPCs? Pros: reuse infra. Cons: different retention/ordering requirements.

Fallback modes (operational playbook):
- Node A unreachable during request -> try B (replica) with prefer_stale_reads=true; if not available, fast-recompute and mark metric: generation_from_scratch.
- Control-plane loses contact with cluster -> nodes continue serving with leases until TTL; if TTL expires, sessions become read-only (safe default).

Implementation notes / incremental rollout plan:
1) Start with a purely client-side lease check + invalidate_token that is stored in a central metadata store (fast KV like etcd). No snapshot transfer initially; nodes will fall back to recompute on miss. (low risk)
2) Add delta log + SnapshotFetch for handoff for a subset of tenants (opt-in). Measure memory and latency impact.
3) Implement optional strong path (roundtrip owner confirmation) behind a per-route flag in Console.

Telemetry to collect early (metrics & traces):
- local_kv_hit_rate_per_session, remote_fetch_latency_p50/p95/p99, lease_acquire_latency, handoff_duration, regeneration_invalidate_count, fallback_recompute_count
- traces need tags: session_id, model, tenant, route, owner_node, request_node, lease_id, invalidate_token

Short ascii diagram - role relationships:

   +------------+      lease     +------------+     snapshot/deltas     +------------+
   |  Ingress   |  <---------->  |  Owner A   |  ---------------------> |  Requester |
   |  (unaffil) |                +------------+                         +------------+
         ^                                                                (may be B)
         |                                                                
     route decisions                                                       
         |                                                               
   +------------+                                                         
   |  Control   |  ------ owner mapping / handoff commands --------------> 
   |  Plane     |                                                         
   +------------+                                                         
Notes: keep ascii diagrams small; they help ops folks grok the flow quickly.

Todo / action items:
- [ ] Draft a small JSON wire spec for LeaseAcquire/LeaseRefresh/GetKV that infra can stub out (assign to Ethan)
- [ ] Add metrics instrumentation plan to RT ticket (assign to Priya)
- [ ] Run small chaos experiment: kill owner node during active session and measure fallbacks and handoff time (SRE)
- [ ] Decide on default max_stale_age_ms for hosted API (product + SRE call)

Random thoughts (brain-dump):
- Maybe we can leverage the existing prefix cache key format and attach a tiny 16-bit epoch to each cache entry to reduce RPC size on verification.
- Keep the protocol resilient to clock skew: all ordering relies on epochs/invalidates, not timestamps.
- For Private deployments with HSM/KMS, we should avoid central metadata writes under heavy load; offer a "local-only" mode where owner annotation is per-VPC and replicated via the customer's control plane.

References / links mentioned in here:
- ENGINF-5123 (design spike)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Slack: #serving-runtime (thread: lease-proto-discuss, ts:2024-11-20 16:02 UTC)

End of scratch notes. Keep this loose — turning this into a formal design doc will require tightening the API shapes and adding state diagrams for every failure mode.
